_meta.indication: Treatment of human smallpox disease caused by variola virus in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 13 kg

pivotal_trials.trial_name: NHP/MPXV (non-human primate/monkeypox virus) animal efficacy studies (Animal Rule surrogate model)
pivotal_trials.phase: Animal efficacy studies conducted under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I)
pivotal_trials.design: Four randomized, placebo-controlled NHP/MPXV studies (three of four double-blinded); tecovirimat started at the time of lesion onset (Day 4 after virus inoculation)
pivotal_trials.population: Cynomolgus macaques challenged intravenously with a high viral challenge dose of 5 x 10^7 plaque-forming units (PFU) of the MPXV Zaire '79 strain
pivotal_trials.n: Four NHP/MPXV studies (numerical per-arm sizes not stated in review summary)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant treatment benefit over placebo for the primary endpoint of mortality when tecovirimat was dosed at 3, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for 14 days starting Day 4; 10 mg/kg/day selected as the fully effective dose

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Rabbit/RPXV (rabbit/rabbitpox virus) animal efficacy study (Animal Rule surrogate model)
pivotal_trials.phase: Animal efficacy study conducted under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled pivotal efficacy study; tecovirimat started at time of fever onset
pivotal_trials.population: 16-week-old New Zealand white rabbits challenged intradermally with 1,000 PFU of the RPXV Utrecht strain
pivotal_trials.n: Two rabbit/RPXV studies (one pivotal placebo-controlled efficacy study; per-arm sizes not stated in review summary)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant treatment benefit over placebo for the primary endpoint of mortality when tecovirimat was dosed at 20, 40, 80, or 120 mg/kg/day for 14 days starting day 4; 40 mg/kg/day selected as the fully effective dose

key_safety: Favorable safety profile; common adverse reactions (>2%) in Study 246-008 (tecovirimat N=359 vs placebo N=90): headache 44 (12%) vs 7 (8%), nausea 16 (5%) vs 4 (4%), abdominal pain 7 (2%) vs 1 (1%), vomiting 7 (2%) vs 0 (0%), diarrhea 7 (2%) vs 2 (2%); one death (pulmonary embolism), the only SAE, not judged related to tecovirimat
target_moa: Tecovirimat is an inhibitor of the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope wrapping protein; it targets and inhibits VP37 and blocks its interaction with cellular Rab9 GTPase and TIP47, preventing formation of egress-competent enveloped virions needed for cell-to-cell and long-range dissemination of virus
modality: Small molecule (oral antiviral; immediate release capsules containing tecovirimat monohydrate equivalent to 200 mg of tecovirimat)

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee meeting convened May 1, 2018; voted unanimously (17-0) that the risk-benefit profile of tecovirimat is acceptable for the treatment of human smallpox

description.text: Added new dosing recommendations for smallpox treatment in adult and pediatric patients weighing 120 kg or more

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for new dosing recommendations for the treatment of human smallpox disease in adult and pediatric patients who weigh 120 kg or more.

description.text: Added new dosage form TPOXX (tecovirimat) 200 mg injection for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 3 kg who are unable to tolerate oral dosing

citations.quote: - Addition of data to support a new dosage form, TPOXX (tecovirimat) 200 mg injection, for use in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 3 kg who are unable to tolerate oral dosing

surrogate_endpoint.text: Not accelerated approval; approved under the Animal Rule (21 CFR 314 Subpart I). Effectiveness established on the primary endpoint of mortality in two lethal surrogate orthopoxvirus animal models (NHP/monkeypox and rabbit/rabbitpox)

citations.quote: It is approved, under the provisions of 21 CFR 314, Subpart I (Approval of New Drugs When Human Efficacy Studies Are Not Ethical or Feasible), effective on the date of this letter
Treatment efficacy was clearly demonstrated using two lethal, well-characterized animal models of non-variola orthopoxvirus infection with disease characteristics relevant to human smallpox.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Under Subpart I, a postmarketing field study (PMR 3417-1) is required, when feasible and ethical, to evaluate clinical response, drug concentrations, and safety of tecovirimat in subjects with variola virus infection

citations.quote: Therefore, you are required to conduct the following postmarketing study, when feasible and ethical, to meet the Subpart I approval requirements:
3417-1 Conduct a Field Study to evaluate the clinical response, drug concentrations, and safety profile of tecovirimat when used in the treatment of subjects with variola virus infection.

Milestone regulatory events included the granting of Fast Track designation in 2005 and Orphan Drug designation in 2006, an FDA Public Workshop in 2009, an Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting in 2011, and the granting of Rolling Review in 2017.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation granted in 2006 for smallpox; product exempt from PREA pediatric assessment requirements

citations.quote: Milestone regulatory events included the granting of Fast Track designation in 2005 and Orphan Drug designation in 2006, an FDA Public Workshop in 2009, an Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting in 2011, and the granting of Rolling Review in 2017.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: Tecovirimat was developed under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I) because clinical efficacy trials for smallpox are not feasible and human challenge studies are unethical; it received Fast Track designation in 2005, Orphan Drug designation in 2006, and Rolling Review in 2017. Effectiveness was established on the primary endpoint of mortality in NHP/monkeypox and rabbit/rabbitpox surrogate models, and the Antimicrobial/Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee voted unanimously (17-0) for approval; the sponsor was granted a material threat medical countermeasure priority review voucher.

citations.quote: tecovirimat was developed under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I), which supports a regulatory approval pathway in which studies using suitable animal models contribute directly to dr

Milestone regulatory events included the granting of Fast Track designation in 2005 and Orphan Drug designation in 2006, an FDA Public Workshop in 2009, an Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee meeting in 2011, and the granting of Rolling Review in 2017.
The Advisory Committee voted unanimously (17-0) that based on the available data, the risk-benefit profile of tecovirimat is acceptable for the treatment of human smallpox.
We also inform you that you have been granted a material threat medical countermeasure priority review voucher (PRV), as provided under section 565A of the FDCA.
